name: Steal War
description: War variant where players can steal cards from opponents. More strategic than classic War.

overview.description: War variant where players can steal cards from opponents. More strategic than classic War.

history.origins: Reported by Gary Philippy and Hayes Ruberti; hybrid of War and Stealing Bundles.
timeline: 20th–21st century: variant reported by Gary Philippy and Hayes Ruberti; combines War with Stealing Bundles mechanic.
history.cultural: Played as a strategic variant of War; no specific regional or cultural tradition documented in sources.
history.evolution: Variant reported by Gary Philippy and Hayes Ruberti; combines standard War (three face-down, one face-up per war) with the stealing mechanic from Stealing Bundles, in which a matching rank captures an opponent's face-up pile.

setup.players: Two players. Each has a face-down packet of 27 cards (half the deck); no hand is held. Both look at the top card before playing and may use it to battle or to steal the opponent's face-up capture pile if the rank matches.
setup.dealing: Deal out all cards evenly so each player has 27 cards in a face-down packet.

rules.objective: Win all the cards. A player who runs out of cards during a war loses immediately.
rules.gameplay: War variant: each player has a face-down packet and a face-up capture pile. Turn your top card; higher card wins the battle and takes the cards to your capture pile (winner chooses which card goes on top). Equal cards trigger a war: three face down, one face up; higher of the face-up cards wins all. If your card's rank matches the top of an opponent's capture pile you may steal that pile instead of playing to the battle. When your packet is empty, shuffle your capture pile to form a new packet.
keyRules: Deck has two jokers; they are the highest cards.
Won cards go on your face-up capture pile; winner may choose which new card is on top.
Matching rank to opponent's pile top allows stealing that pile instead of playing to battle.
Card played and released cannot be used to steal; playing a card that matches your own pile top protects your pile from being stolen that turn.
Running out of cards during a war means immediate loss.

strategy.basic: Choose when to play a card to the battle versus when to steal an opponent's pile; stealing a small pile may be less valuable than winning a war.
strategy.intermediate: Track the top card of each capture pile so you know when you can steal. Prefer stealing when the opponent's pile is large; prefer playing to the battle when you can win the war or when your card is strong.
strategy.advanced: Weigh the expected value of stealing a pile versus winning the current battle or war. Protect your own pile by playing a card that matches your pile top when the opponent could otherwise steal it.
tips: You may deliberately play your card to the battle rather than stealing with it, for example to win a war instead of stealing a small pile.

variations.name: Protection rule
variations.description: Playing a card that matches your own pile top protects that pile from being stolen during that turn (resolves timing when both players could steal).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Protection rule only clarifies turn order; no engine parameter overrides needed.

scoring.description: Winner is the player who collects all the cards; a player who runs out of cards during a war loses immediately.
scoring.winCondition: Collect all the cards; running out of cards during a war means immediate loss.
